- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25 or -1.00), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70% from prior 10d), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 30d moving average to dampen.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.33 or +1.00), model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 3–5% to align with mean reversion.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or low; increase forecast by 2–5% if recent 18d mean is >70.
- For 30d horizon, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model fails to adjust; apply 3–5% downward correction immediately after sentiment flip.
